claims.value: The constitution effective from May 1947 established popular sovereignty. The emperor became a symbol of the state, while the Diet consisted of the House of Representatives and House of Councillors. The cabinet exercised executive authority and was collectively responsible to the Diet. Hirohito continued in the imperial office, but its constitutional meaning differed from the Meiji framework. Prime ministerial changes are shown separately; this continuity of a person is not continuity of the earlier system of imperial sovereignty. These domestic constitutional institutions operated during the Allied occupation, under the authority of the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers.

claims.value: The peace treaty took effect on 28 April 1952, ending the Allied occupation and restoring Japan to sovereign equality. The 1947 constitution continued to place sovereignty in the people, with an emperor who symbolised the state, a bicameral Diet and a cabinet responsible to it. This post-occupation setting differs both from the earlier imperial framework and from the first years of the new constitution under occupation. Changes of prime minister are recorded separately.
